summary: Soshū Nishioka worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was attested as a professor at International Buddhist University in 2000 and 2015.

Sotan Oka was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Teizo Shiratori, and Fusho Nagano. He served at Komazawa University as dean/professor in 1899 and president in 1918, and he founded Antai-ji in 1921.

Soyen Shaku worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies, studying at Keio University and under several masters including Kosen Imakita. He served at Nagata Zendo, Engaku-ji as Zen master, and Hanazono University as president (1914–1917).

Sras Rinpoche III is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery and Gyume Tantric Monastery. He served at Rizong Monastery, Drepung Loseling Monastery, and Gyume Tantric Monastery.

Sravana Borkataky-Varma specializes in religious studies and Indology, earning degrees from the University of Delhi and Rice University (PhD). She has taught at Rice, Montana, UNC Wilmington, Harvard (Fellow), and the University of Houston.

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. Educated at Andhra University, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Marburg (PhD), he served as a professor at Aligarh Muslim University from around 1977 to 1997.
Sri Anirvan worked in Indology and philosophy. He completed his studies at the University of Dhaka, Sanskrit College and University, and the University of Calcutta between 1911 and 1918.

Srikanth Kaul was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. In 1967, he was attested at Government Degree College, Sopore, and as a professor at the Research and Archaeological Department, Jammu and Kashmir.

Srinivas H. Ritti was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He served as an Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (1964) and Government Epigraphist for India (1965), and as professor at Karnatak University (attested 1975).
Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan was an Indology scholar who earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg. He served as Privatdozent for Indology at the University of Hamburg from 1973 to 1997.

Srisa Chandra Vasu was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Rang Mahal School and Government College University, Lahore. He served as a Vakil at Allahabad High Court, became a Fellow of the University of Allahabad, and founded Panini Office.

Stacey Van Vleet specializes in Tibetology, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Colorado and Columbia University under Carole McGranahan and Tashi Tsering Josayma, and held a post at Columbia University in 2013.

Stamford Raffles worked in history/archaeology and linguistics. He served with the East India Company, as Lieutenant-governor of Java and British Bencoolen, and founded and served as president of the Zoological Society of London.

Stanislas Julien studied at Collège de France under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat. He held the Chair of Chinese at Collège de France (1832–1873) and posts at the Institut de France, Bibliothèque nationale de France, and Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales.

Stanislav Grof studied at the University of Prague. He held psychiatric posts in the Czech Republic and Maryland, followed by appointments at Johns Hopkins University, Esalen Institute (1973–1987), and California Institute of Integral Studies (1994–2015).

Stanisław Schayer worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He founded and served as a professor at the University of Warsaw in 1922 and was a member of the Warsaw Scientific Society and Polish Academy of Arts and Sciences.
Stanley Abe is a scholar in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held an attested academic post at Duke University in 1995 and 2004.
Stanley Cecil Sutton worked in history/archaeology and Indology. He served as Librarian at the Commonwealth Relations Office (attested 1953) and at the India Office Library (attested 1974).

Stanley Insler studied at Columbia, Tübingen, and Yale under Paul Thieme. A specialist in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he served as Edward E. Salisbury Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Yale (1976–2012).
Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah studied at Ceylon, Cornell, and Harvard. He taught at Ceylon, Cambridge, Chicago, and Harvard, where he was Esther and Sidney Rabb Professor (Emeritus) of Anthropology.
